title: Subjunctive Mood
description: Master the subjunctive mood for Grade 12: formulaic, mandative and hypothetical subjunctive, and 'as if/as though' — for formal and hypothetical English, with bilingual notes and tests.

topics.title: Mandative & Hypothetical Subjunctive
topics.concept:
The mandative subjunctive follows verbs and adjectives of demand, suggestion, recommendation and necessity. The 'that-clause' uses the base verb for all subjects (no -s, no 'should' in formal style):

  • Verbs: suggest, recommend, demand, insist, propose, request, order.
    I suggest that she write the letter. / They demanded that he be released.
  • Adjectives: It is essential/important/necessary/vital that…
    It is essential that every member attend.

The hypothetical subjunctive uses were for all subjects in unreal/imaginary clauses after if, wish, suppose, would rather:

  • If I were rich… / I wish I were taller. / I'd rather you were here.

examples.problem: Complete: The doctor recommended that he ___ (take) rest.
examples.solution: take — mandative subjunctive uses the base verb, even with 'he'.
were — hypothetical subjunctive uses 'were' for all subjects.

recap: Mandative: after suggest/demand/insist… use the base verb (he go, he be)
Hypothetical: use 'were' for all subjects in unreal clauses

topics.title: Formulaic Subjunctive & As If / As Though
topics.concept:
The formulaic (fixed) subjunctive survives in set phrases that express a wish or blessing:

  • Long live the Queen! / God save the king! / Come what may. / Be that as it may. / So be it. / Heaven forbid! / Suffice it to say…

as if / as though introduces an unreal comparison; for something untrue now, use the past form, with were for all subjects:

  • He talks as if he were the boss. (he isn't)
  • She spends money as though there were no tomorrow.

(When the comparison is likely true, ordinary tenses are used: It looks as if it is going to rain.)

Note: in everyday informal English, 'was' often replaces the subjunctive 'were' — but formal writing and exams expect 'were'.

examples.problem: Complete: He behaves as though he ___ (own) the place.
examples.solution: owned — an unreal comparison uses the past subjunctive.

examples.problem: Identify the formulaic subjunctive: Come what may, I will stand by you.
examples.solution: 'Come what may' — a fixed subjunctive expression.

recap: Formulaic: fixed phrases (Long live…, Come what may, So be it)
as if/as though + past (were) for something untrue now
Formal English keeps 'were'; informal often uses 'was'

'He talks as if he ___ a scholar.'
'The doctor advised that the patient ___ rest.'

questions.explanation: The mandative subjunctive after 'imperative that' uses the base verb 'submit'.

questions.explanation: 'Were it not for your help' / 'If it were not for…' uses 'were'.

options: Be that as it may, we proceed.
questions.explanation: 'Be that as it may' is a fixed subjunctive.

questions.q: Choose the correct mandative form: 'I move that the motion ___ adopted.'
Rearrange: 'essential / it / he / that / present / is / be'
options: It is essential that he be present.
It is essential he is present that.
He is essential that it be present.
That he be present it is essential.
questions.explanation: 'It is essential that he be present.'

questions.q: Which sentence keeps the subjunctive consistently?
options: The chair asked that the report be revised and that it is resubmitted.
The chair asked that the report be revised and resubmitted.
The chair asked that the report is revised and be resubmitted.
The chair asked that the report being revised and resubmitted.
questions.explanation: Both verbs take the base form: 'be revised and resubmitted'.

outcomes: Recognise the three kinds of subjunctive
Use the mandative subjunctive after verbs of demand/suggestion
Use the hypothetical subjunctive (were) for unreal situations
Use 'as if / as though' with the subjunctive

intro.en: The subjunctive mood expresses things that are not facts — wishes, demands, suggestions and hypotheticals. Its signature move is the bare base verb after certain verbs (I suggest that she go) and were for all subjects in unreal clauses (If I were you…). It is the most formal corner of English grammar — and a marker of polished writing.
intro.hi: संभावनार्थक भाव (subjunctive mood) उन बातों को व्यक्त करता है जो तथ्य नहीं हैं — इच्छाएँ, माँगें, सुझाव और काल्पनिक स्थितियाँ। इसकी पहचान है कुछ क्रियाओं के बाद मूल क्रिया (I suggest that she go) और unreal उपवाक्यों में सभी subjects के लिए were (If I were you…)। यह अंग्रेज़ी व्याकरण का सबसे औपचारिक कोना है — और परिष्कृत लेखन की पहचान।

real_life.situation:
A formal recommendation:

Casual: I think she should be present.
Subjunctive: I insist that she be present.
real_life.why: After 'insist', the verb takes the bare form 'be' (not 'is' or 'should be') — that is the mandative subjunctive. It sounds firm and formal, exactly the tone official writing demands.

common_mistakes.note: Mandative subjunctive uses the base verb.

common_mistakes.right: It is essential that she be present.

reading.passage: The committee insisted that every proposal be reviewed twice. "It is essential," said the chair, "that no decision be rushed." One member spoke as if he were already certain of the outcome, but the others recommended that he wait. "Come what may," the chair concluded, "I move that the vote be postponed." So be it, they agreed.

questions.q: Identify two mandative subjunctives and explain the verb form.
questions.answer: 'every proposal be reviewed', 'no decision be rushed', 'he wait', 'the vote be postponed' — all use the base verb after demand/recommend.

questions.q: Find the unreal comparison and explain 'were'.
questions.answer: 'as if he were already certain' — he is not certain, so the past subjunctive 'were' is used.
'Come what may' and 'So be it' — fixed subjunctive expressions.

speaking: I suggest that he be careful.
It is essential that we act now.
If I were you, I would wait.
He talks as if he knew everything.
Come what may, we shall succeed.

writing.prompt: Write five formal sentences: two with the mandative subjunctive (suggest/demand/essential), two with the hypothetical subjunctive (if I were / I wish I were), and one formulaic expression.
writing.example: I insist that he be present. It is vital that she be informed. If I were rich, I would help. I wish I were braver. So be it.
